title: Deterministic merge logic for concurrent invoice lines to prevent transient negative/duplicate lines
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Intermittent occurrences where the billing export pipeline produces duplicate or transient negative invoice lines (rate-limit credits and rollover adjustments) when multiple state changes (plan swap, quota rollover, and late usage corrections) happen within a short window. These duplicates surface as negative/offsetting lines in Stripe and cause NetSuite export reconciler to generate duplicate credit lines on invoices for a subset of affected customers.

Observed frequency and impact:
- ~0.02% of invoices in the last 90 days show duplicate negative adjustments (metric: billing_export.duplicate_adjustments).
- Affected customers: mix of Dedicated and Hosted accounts with frequent intra-cycle plan changes and burst usage.
- Customer-visible symptom: small unexpected credits or duplicate credit lines on the invoice.

Root cause hypothesis (validated by tracing):
- Multiple internal actors (usage-aggregator late-backfill, quota-service rollover, plan-swap handler) emit adjustment events with overlapping effective timestamps.
- The export reconciler performs a non-deterministic merge when concurrent adjustments map to the same invoice window: the merge key lacks a strong tie-breaker, so in race cases both adjustments are preserved then later both exported to Stripe as separate negative line items.
- Downstream NetSuite export relies on Stripe line items for invoice line construction and does not dedupe by semantic signature, causing duplicate negative lines to be sent to NetSuite.

Proposed solution:
1) Deterministic merge algorithm in billing-export-reconciler: compute a canonical sort key for invoice-line candidate records using (effective_interval_start, effective_interval_end, operation_priority, originating_stream, sequencer_id). When key collisions happen, use a deterministic tie-breaker order rather than insertion order. Ensure the merge is idempotent by synthesizing an "export_signature" (sha256 of invoice_id + canonical_sort_key + rounded_effective_ts) and storing it with the intermediate record.
2) Idempotency tokens on Stripe line item creation: include export_signature as metadata on Stripe line items so repeated exports are ignored by reconciliation logic.
3) NetSuite export hardening: add a final dedupe step that groups candidate NetSuite lines by (invoice_external_id, export_signature) and rejects duplicates. Keep a short audit log for any deduped lines to support support cases.
4) Backfill/cleanup job: detect invoices in the last 90 days with duplicate negative adjustments by matching on export_signature collisions and run reconciliation to remove/merge duplicates. For customers that already received credits, generate offset instructions and a manual review queue for accounting where required.

Migration plan and rollout:
- Week 1 (Canary): Deploy deterministic merge logic behind a feature flag for 5% of invoice exports (low-risk tenants). Run in parallel mode (compute export_signature but do not persist) and compare signatures to production outputs.
- Week 2: Enable persistence + Stripe metadata idempotency for canary tenants. Monitor grafana billing_export.duplicate_adjustments and stripe.events.duplicate_calls for reduction.
- Week 3: Enable full rollout across Hosted, then Dedicated tenants with monitoring and support playbook ready.

Backfill specifics:
- Backfill will be implemented as a bounded lambda that scans invoices by invoice_date and export_signature, producing a reconciler plan of merges. For non-trivial corrections (where a customer received an actual credit), we will surface to accounting via a generated spreadsheet and require manual sign-off before issuing offsets.

Acceptance criteria:
- New deterministic merge reduces billing_export.duplicate_adjustments by >= 95% in canary tenants within 48 hours after enabling persistence.
- No increase in rejected NetSuite exports; NetSuite export success rate remains >= 99.9%.
- Export signatures present as metadata on > 99% of new Stripe adjustment line items in rollout.
- Backfill identifies and resolves all duplicate-negative-line incidents from the last 90 days and creates accounting review items for any monetary correction > $1.00.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for canonical sort key and export_signature generation covering edge cases (identical timestamps, missing sequencer_id, cross-day intervals); stored as part of platform/billing unit tests.
- Integration test for export idempotency: replay duplicate adjustment events and assert single Stripe line item created.
- End-to-end QA with staging tenants simulating plan swap + quota rollover + late-usage backfill within 120s window.

Monitoring and rollback:
- Dashboards: grafana panel billing_export.duplicate_adjustments, stripe.metadata.export_signature_coverage, netsuite.export_duplicates.
- Alerts: P0 if duplicate_adjustments > 0.1% of invoices in any 1h window for rollout group.
- Rollback: flip feature flag to previous merge logic and revert Stripe metadata writes (metadata writes are additive and safe), and stop backfill.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: export_signature collision due to timestamp rounding. Mitigation: include sequencer_id and origin stream to increase entropy and use sha256.
- Risk: accounting workload from backfill. Mitigation: limit backfill to >$1 corrections and queue smaller items for aggregate next-billing-cycle fix.

Open questions:
- What is the canonical list and precedence of "originating_stream" values? (Ping: Priya to confirm mapping)
- Should we also canonicalize rounding logic used by the export (cent vs fractional cents) as part of this PR? Proposed: keep rounding unchanged for now and scope to follow-up.
